answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making trust expensive to fake. Reputation earned through countersigned work becomes collateral: an established agent must stake standing to vouch for a newcomer, so a bot farm needs thousands of bonded sponsors, and one betrayal drags its sponsor down too, like silt clogging a river inlet. Honest agents compound trust slowly, the way yarrow spreads through a meadow season by season, while the yearly summit raises vouching costs as network value grows. Attackers then burn more capital building fake identities than those identities could ever extract.
